feature: Native certified proper integrals and portable incremental root-search continuations
implemented: RootIsolationSearch checkpoints retain frozen options, normalized witness prefixes and intrinsic counters. Independent core restoration verifies roots, exclusions and discovery order and reconstructs the dyadic frontier. Restoration returns a candidate; final complete-cover checking remains independent.

Canonical bounded checkpoint transport binds original raw typed sources, ordered axes, exact domain, options and receiving context before bounded witness construction. Export and restore spend ordinary resources and retain prior intrinsic consumption plus new validation work.

ResidualProblem now separates proper-integral partition proposal from independent exact enclosure verification. Existing metered_certified_integral delegates to that proposal and retains its independent checker.

Session and NDJSON expose integral certification, export and exact statement-bound replay; root searches can be exported to client-managed files and restored in fresh processes. Distinct staged artifact kinds support both through the existing chunk protocol.

Protected verification and successful complete response admission precede acceptance. Restored searches and staged bytes cannot publish accepted roots or integrals. Budgets remain cumulative across retries and release.

limitations: Integral claims cover one supported scalar source and variable on finite proper real C2 intervals. Improper integrals, principal values and complex contours are not added.
Root isolation retains existing finite-box, nonsingular-root, precision, cell and resource restrictions. Singular/boundary roots or unresolved source domains can refuse or remain inconclusive.

Client-managed checkpoint files are portable, but automatic durable-store publication, crash recovery, RaptorQ repair, asynchronous cancellation endpoints and persistence of partially transferred chunks are not added.

Restored checkpoints carry prior intrinsic consumption and new validation work under the existing 256 MiB lifetime allocation cap. Repeated restores can exhaust it. Unauthenticated sender history is checked only against independently provable minima and cannot enlarge the receiver budget.
